speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if you notice any redness, warmth, or drainage? Also, do you have any history of diabetes or circulation issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your family history of leg swelling and your prior DVT, could you tell me if the wound is located on the medial (inner) aspect of your right ankle? Also, have you noticed any varicose veins or skin discoloration like brown staining in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency with Venous Stasis Ulcer. The clinical picture of a 6-month non-healing wound on the right lower leg, combined with a decade of chronic edema, a history of DVT, and positive family history, strongly points to venous hypertension as the primary etiology. REQUEST IMAGES: Lower_extremity_ultrasound (duplex) to confirm chronic DVT or valvular incompetence.
